title: Matar Paneer

ingredients.title: For the Paneer & Peas
items: Paneer (cottage cheese) – 250 g, cut into 1-inch cubes
Green peas – 1 cup, fresh or frozen
Oil or ghee – 1–2 tsp, for sautéing

ingredients.title: For the Spices
items: Red chili powder – 1 tsp, adjust to taste

ingredients.title: For Finishing
items: Fresh cream – ½ cup, or yogurt – 2 tbsp (optional)
Fresh coriander leaves – chopped, for garnish

instruction.title: Prepare the Paneer & Peas
steps: Heat 1–2 tsp oil or ghee in a pan over medium heat.
Lightly sauté the paneer cubes until golden on all sides, if desired.
Remove the paneer and set aside.
If using fresh peas, blanch them in boiling water for 2–3 minutes and drain. Frozen peas can be added directly.

instruction.title: Prepare the Masala Base
steps: Heat 2 tsp oil or ghee in the same pan.
Add cumin seeds and let them crackle.
Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
Add ginger-garlic paste and sauté for 1–2 minutes until the raw aroma disappears.
Add tomato puree, turmeric, red chili powder, coriander powder, and cumin powder.
Cook until the tomatoes are fully reduced and the oil begins to separate from the masala.

instruction.title: Cook the Curry
steps: Add about 1 cup water and stir to form a smooth gravy.
Add the green peas and sautéed paneer cubes.
Simmer over low-medium heat for 5–7 minutes so the peas cook and the paneer absorbs the gravy.
Add garam masala and crushed kasuri methi.
Stir gently to avoid breaking the paneer.
For a richer curry, stir in fresh cream or whisked yogurt.
Adjust the consistency with additional water if needed.

instruction.title: Garnish & Serve
steps: Turn off the heat and garnish with freshly chopped coriander leaves.
Serve hot with naan, roti, or steamed basmati rice.

chefTips: Paneer: Use fresh, soft paneer for the best creamy texture.
Paneer texture: Avoid over-frying the cubes, as prolonged frying can make paneer firm and chewy.
Kasuri methi: Crush the dried fenugreek leaves between your palms before adding to release their aroma.
Spices: Lightly roasting whole spices before grinding can add extra depth to the masala.
Yogurt: If using yogurt instead of cream, whisk it well and add over low heat to reduce the chance of curdling.
Gravy: Adjust the water according to whether you prefer a thick restaurant-style curry or a lighter gravy.
